summary: OUTPOST is an interactive game for young scientists aged 7 to 12 to immerse themselves in the world of space exploration. It features a plethora of educational tools, such as a breakdown of mineral compositions in Martian soil and real-world data sprinkled throughout each feature. Our website features data from various instruments, such as the Mars Climate Sounder, which provided important data on Martian temperatures at numerous geographical locations, compiled with interactive games and quizzes to provide an engaging and informative experience of the trade-offs real-world scientists and engineers must make.
details:
OUTPOST is an interactive online game that allows users to simulate what it’s like to command an outpost on Mars. By completing three missions involving real-world decision-making scenarios and exploring activities based on authentic NASA datasets, players can deepen their understanding of NASA’s Mars exploration Missions in a fun and accessible way. As they progress, players can gain experience points (XP) and unlock new ranks, going from a Space Cadet all the way to a Mission Commander.

Players progress through three missions, completing tasks and making decisions to manage their Martian outpost. They can also explore the Sky Lab and Rock Lab, where they interact with real NASA datasets through graphs, experiments, and quizzes, including the "Hot or Cold?" temperature challenges. Additionally, players can browse an interactive album featuring images of Mars, test their knowledge through various quizzes throughout the game, and explore the Sky Lab and Rock Lab to dive into information from NASA’s Reconnaissance Orbiter and Curiosity Rover.

OUTPOST balances its engagement and detail by dividing a substantial amount of NASA data into separate games and activities all available on the same website, whether that be through the multiple labs, quizzes, or decision-based games. This way, young learners can experience running a Martian outpost while still being able to digest real-life data through gamification and hands-on exploration. OUTPOST allows users to develop their data interpretation and critical thinking skills in a fun way, rather than simply reading about previous Martian missions. 

We created OUTPOST to make space exploration engaging and accessible to young learners from the comfort of their own home. We want players to be able to gain a practical understanding of why facts and figures about Mars are significant through managing their own outpost rather than consuming information in a way that’s hard to comprehend, let alone to remember or to utilise. Ultimately, we hope to spark curiosity about STEM and demonstrate how real-world engineering decisions made under pressure and constraints can shape the success of space exploration.

For web development, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were used. To allow for shared collaboration on the project amongst our team’s frontend and backend developers, GitHub was used. The programming was done in VS Code, and the website was deployed through Vercel. To aid with programming and debugging, Claude Code was used, as well as ChatGPT.
